security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting false positives, including backticks around tool names, paths, settings, and JSON examples. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious execution intent was found, but the skill does direct agents to unpinned remote fallback instruction files.

remediation.issue: Remote fallback instructions are loaded from live main-branch URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Pin fallback URLs to immutable commit hashes or bundle the referenced sibling skill documents in the package.

remediation.issue: Sibling skill references use ../ paths outside the current skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Keep all referenced instruction files inside the distributed skill package, or clearly require user confirmation before reading external references.

remediation.issue: CloudBase Run write actions include deploy, download, and delete workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the existing explicit confirmation requirement for delete and require users to approve production-impacting deploy actions.

content.value_statement: CloudBase Run projects require clear mode, access, and deployment choices. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through reliable CloudBase Run backend workflows.
actual_capabilities: Helps choose CloudBase Run Function mode or Container mode for a backend service.
Lists runtime rules for PORT, stateless services, dependency size, and CPU memory ratios.
Routes CloudBase Run read and write tasks to queryCloudRun and manageCloudRun actions.
Provides access guidance for public web, Mini Program, private, and VPC services.
Includes initialization, local run, deployment, and troubleshooting guidance for CloudBase Run services.
limitations: It does not provide CloudBase account permissions or deployment credentials.
Container mode local run is not supported by the described tool flow.
It does not cover database schema design or frontend-only projects.
Some fallback reference links point to external CloudBase skill documents that may change.

use_cases.title: Launch a streaming backend
use_cases.description: Choose the right CloudBase Run mode and deploy an HTTP, SSE, or WebSocket backend.

use_cases.title: Move a container service
use_cases.description: Prepare a container-based service for CloudBase Run with correct port, access, and resource settings.

use_cases.title: Create an Agent service
use_cases.description: Use Function mode CloudBase Run guidance for Agent service creation and deployment checks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a CloudBase Run mode
prompt_templates.prompt: Use cloudrun-development to decide whether my backend should use Function mode or Container mode. Explain the tradeoffs for my service requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize a Function mode service
prompt_templates.prompt: Use cloudrun-development to initialize a CloudBase Run Function mode service for an HTTP API. Include the required runtime checks before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy with access controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Use cloudrun-development to deploy my CloudBase Run service with the correct public, Mini Program, private, or VPC access model.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a failed deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use cloudrun-development to inspect my failed CloudBase Run deployment, review deploy logs, and propose fixes for runtime, Dockerfile, or resource issues.

output_examples.input: I need a public SSE backend with low startup latency.
output: Recommend Function mode because the service uses streaming and does not require a custom container.
Use public web access only after confirming the authentication flow.
Set minimum instances above zero if the user accepts the added cost.

output_examples.input: My CloudBase Run deploy failed after a Dockerfile change.
output: Inspect the latest deployment log before changing configuration.
Check that the container listens on the platform port.
Verify the CPU and memory ratio before redeploying.

output_examples.input: I want to delete an old CloudBase Run service.
output: Ask for explicit confirmation before deletion.
Verify the target service name and environment.
Use the delete operation only after the user confirms the destructive action.

best_practices: Choose Function mode or Container mode before creating project files.
Keep services stateless and store durable data in managed storage.
Verify access type and deployment details before public use.
anti_patterns: Using CloudBase Run for simple tasks that fit a cloud function.
Opening public access when private or Mini Program access is enough.
Assuming Container mode can use local run tooling.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when building, deploying, inspecting, or debugging a CloudBase Run backend service.

faq.question: Does it support both CloudBase Run modes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when to use Function mode and when Container mode is a better fit.

faq.question: Can it deploy a service for me?
faq.answer: It can guide managed CloudBase Run deployment actions when the required tools and permissions are available.

faq.question: Does it handle delete operations safely?
faq.answer: The skill states that delete operations require explicit confirmation and the force setting.

faq.question: Is it useful for frontend-only projects?
faq.answer: No. It is intended for backend services, not frontend-only projects.

faq.question: Does it include troubleshooting guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers access failures, deployment failures, local run limits, and performance issues.
